Non-contiguous Kafka offsets stall commits permanently for the partition
get_committable_offsets walks range(start, max_offset+1) and breaks at the first offset not in all_offsets. After the first commit, start is last_committed+1, so the tracker requires every following offset to be seen. Kafka offsets can have gaps (compacted topics, transaction control markers, filtered or dropped messages not routed through submit). If offset 101 is never submitted, 100 is committed and the loop breaks at 101 on every later pass. The gap is never skipped, so highest_committable stays at last_committed. The

Graceful shutdown does not drain queues because the worker's shutdown flag is set before the queue shutdown
FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True for every worker, then calls q.shutdown(immediate=False), which is meant to let queued items drain. OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on `while not self.shutdown`. A worker that finishes its current item therefore sees the flag and exits, even though its queue still holds items. Those items are never processed and never completed. Example: a queue holds 100 items when close() runs. The worker finishes the item it is on and returns, leaving t

Failed queue submission marks the offset completed, so unprocessed messages can be committed
FixedQueuePool.submit calls offset_tracker.add_offset and then work_queue.put. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit (lines 317-325) catches any exception from that call and calls add_offset and complete_offset for the message. If put raises, for example queue.ShutDown after FixedQueuePool.shutdown has called q.shutdown(), the work item never reached a worker. Its offset is still marked complete. get_committable_offsets then treats it as processed and the commit loop can commit past it. terminate() does

Commits highest processed offset rather than next offset
The commit loop passes highest_committable, the offset of the last processed message, straight to commit_function. Arroyo and Kafka commit semantics expect the next offset to consume (offset+1). mark_committed also records the same value.
After a restart or rebalance the last processed message of each partition is redelivered and processed again.

Factory-shared FixedQueuePool is shut down by per-assignment strategy close(), then reused after rebalance, silently dropping messages
The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and the same instance is handed to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy built by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker. Arroyo creates a new strategy on each partition assignment and closes the old one on each revocation. OrderedQueueWorker.run completes the offset in a `finally` block (queue_consumer.py:148-149), so an offset whose processor raised still counts as complete. In the test, offset 100 raises and offset 101 succeeds. Both end up complete and contiguous, so get_committable_offsets returns 101.
